requirements.evidence: app/Models/Queue.php:6 and app/Models/Ticket.php:9 import `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\HasFactory`, but HasFactory is the trait `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory`, so `use HasFactory;` fails with 'Trait not found' and neither model can load. app/Models/Ticket.php:14,76 throws `Illuminate\Exceptions\AuthorizationException`, which does not exist (the task names `Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException`). Queue has no casts for `is_active` boolean or `labels_i18n` array (Queue.php:12-31). There is no explicit retry on a unique (queue_id, code) collision: `DB::transaction(..., 3)` at IssueTicket.php:49 retries only on deadlocks. TicketFactory.php:23 creates an extra queue to compute the code, and `forQueue` computes the code at make time, so two tickets made in one batch would both get A001. nextCode takes the numeric max (Ticket.php:53-68) instead of 'last valid by insertion order'. The parts that work: the lock-and-reload of the queue row (IssueTicket.php:34-41), the negative priority check, the creating defaults, and the immutability hook.

conventions.evidence: Tests are a class-based PHPUnit file (tests/Feature/QueueTicketTest.php:16), not Pest as the conventions require (`make:test --pest`). The membership check is hand-rolled inside the model (Ticket.php:75) instead of going through a policy/gate. docs/database-schema.md:478-485 duplicates the `totems` block, adds no `queues` table and indents the closing fence (`    ````), which breaks the code block. CHANGELOG.md is not updated. Import placement in Entity.php:10 does not follow sibling style. The good parts: the domain write goes through `app/Actions/IssueTicket`, both migrations have reversible `down()`, and `$fillable` is set deliberately.

security.evidence: call() is meant to reject non-members (Ticket.php:75-77), but it throws a non-existent class, and it relies on `membershipFor`, a method this diff does not show. Authorization does not go through a policy. Issuance has no authorization (none is required at this layer). Mass assignment: `$fillable` on Ticket includes `status`, `called_by_user_id` and `code` (Ticket.php:17), which is broad but limited by the write-once hook. No user input is rendered.

tests.evidence: QueueTicketTest.php:20 imports `Illuminate\Testing\RefreshDatabase` (the real one is `Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase`), so the test class cannot load. The unauthorized test expects the non-existent `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\AuthorizationException` (line 85). The file ends with a stray `?>` (line 100). Untested: a stale queue instance deactivated after loading, nothing persisted on rejection, negative priority, malformed legacy codes, A999->A1000, no reuse after deletion, the ticket staying unchanged after an unauthorized call, and the factory's `forQueue` and explicit-code behaviour. Several imports are unused (DatabaseFactory, Migration, Blueprint, Schema, EntityMembership).

simplicity.evidence: IssueTicket is short and direct. But the defaults are duplicated between the factory definition and the `creating` hook (Ticket.php:94-112). The factory builds an extra throwaway queue just to compute a code (TicketFactory.php:23) instead of relying on the hook. The redundant casts `'code' => 'string'` and `'called_by_user_id' => 'int'` add noise.

readability.evidence: Unused or non-existent imports: `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Enum` in both enums (TicketChannel.php:5, TicketStatus.php:5), and `HasGuarded`, `HasOne`, `RuntimeException` in Ticket.php:10,13,16. The fully qualified return type at Queue.php:19 duplicates an import that is already there. The `'code' => 'string'` line at Ticket.php:24 is misindented. There is a stray `?>` at the end of the test file. The 'Negative priority' check in the creating hook throws LogicException while the action throws InvalidArgumentException, which is inconsistent.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. The exception is docs/database-schema.md:478-485, which re-adds a duplicate `totems` entity unrelated to this change.

issues.explanation: HasFactory is imported from `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes` instead of `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories`, so `use HasFactory;` causes a fatal 'Trait not found' error and neither model can load.
`Illuminate\Exceptions\AuthorizationException` does not exist; the task requires `Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException`, so an unauthorized call raises an Error instead.
The test imports the wrong RefreshDatabase namespace and expects a non-existent `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\AuthorizationException`, so the suite cannot load or pass.

Most rules are untested: stale-instance rejection, nothing persisted on rejection, negative priority, malformed codes, A1000 rollover, no reuse after deletion, the ticket staying unchanged after an unauthorized call, and factory behaviour; the file is also PHPUnit rather than Pest.

The default definition computes the code from a separate, newly created queue rather than the ticket's queue. `forQueue` computes the code eagerly at make time, so batch creation (count(2)) gives duplicate A001 codes instead of A001/A002.
The required casts (`is_active` => boolean, `labels_i18n` => array) are missing from Queue.
`DB::transaction(..., 3)` retries only on deadlocks, not on the unique (queue_id, code) collision that the task asks to retry on.
nextCode uses the numeric max over all codes instead of the last valid code by insertion order, as the task specifies.
The schema doc gains a duplicate `totems` block and an indented closing fence that breaks the mermaid block, and no `queues` table is documented; CHANGELOG is not updated.
Membership authorization is done ad hoc in the model via an unshown `membershipFor` helper rather than through a policy/gate.
There are unused or non-existent imports and a trailing `?>` in the test file.

review.summary: The change adds migrations, Queue/Ticket models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action with a locked re-read of the queue, and some docs and tests. However, both models import HasFactory from a non-existent namespace, call() throws a non-existent exception class, and the test file uses the wrong RefreshDatabase namespace, so neither the code nor the tests can run. Factories, casts, collision retry, test coverage and docs also need substantial rework before merging.
